Cell 37 quotes exactly as recorded: train_samples=floor(0.8*576)=460, testList=range(461,576), train_set=splits['train'] immediately overwritten by train_set=windows_dataset, and train_test_split(X_train.indices_, test_size=0.2, shuffle=False) over all 576 indices. I re-derived in pure Python: train 0..459 (460), val 460..575 (116), test 461..575 (115), test-and-val overlap 115/115, val-minus-test {460} and 460 mod 12 = 4, so block 456..467 straddles train/val. No cell was executed and the pipeline was not re-run.

The candidate is correct as shipped, not just described. Running the committed seedv_split.py independently: split_indices(48,12) with the default seed 42 returns 348/120/108 over 29/10/9 whole sessions, each list ascending, pairwise intersections empty, and sorted(train+val+test)==range(576). Across the 160 recorded grid inputs (n_sessions 3..59 at trials_per_session 1 and 2; 3..48 at 12) my own checker found 0 failures under non-empty + disjoint + exact-once coverage + whole-session integrity, matching the record's 160/160. n_sessions=3 yields 12/12/12 (1/1/1), so the empty-partition loophole is genuinely closed.

Parent-vs-candidate comparison reproduced. Over N=0..1000 the reconstructed cell-37 split satisfies disjointness+coverage on exactly 6/1001 inputs (N=0..5, all with an empty test set) and 0/1001 once non-emptiness is required; at N=576 it is 460/116/115 with 115/115 overlap and val-only {460}. Those are the figures in research.json, RESEARCH.md and report.json. The candidate's 160/160 grid and the parent's 0/1001 use different, explicitly labelled input domains (the mandated API rejects n_sessions<3), but the conclusion does not rest on that asymmetry: the parent fails for every N>=6 whether or not non-emptiness is required.

Reproducibility evidence is authentic and independently reproducible. Repeated calls are element-wise identical; random.getstate() is unchanged; seed 7 changes membership (test set differs); and the recorded digest 1b8bc0aaeee1afb6055359e283e3a4625887e84082bfa1fef44b1f0285a612e8 is exactly hashlib.sha256(json.dumps((train,val,test)).encode()).hexdigest() and is identical under PYTHONHASHSEED 0, 1 and 12345 (the record does not name json.dumps; see finding 3).

Measurement is fair and honestly labelled. I re-measured with time.perf_counter best-of-5 on this machine: candidate 0.0965 ms vs recorded 0.0758 ms at 48x12; parent 0.0051 ms vs 0.0042 ms; at n=100000 (2500x40) candidate 10.851 ms vs 10.518 ms and parent 0.904 ms vs 0.8738 ms. Same order, machine-specific as stated, and no timing is used as correctness evidence. Peak traced memory at 48x12 reproduced exactly at 42.8984375 KiB, matching the recorded 42.9 KiB.

Input hardening behaves as recorded: NaN, inf, negative, zero, ratio 1.0, summing-to-1.1/0.9, bool and float counts, n_sessions in {0,1,2,-1} and trials_per_session in {0,-1} all raise ValueError; (0.7,0.2,0.1) and (0.3,0.35,0.35) are accepted via math.fsum with 1e-9 tolerance; (0.7,0.2,0.1) at 48x12 gives 396/120/60 as claimed. validate_partition raises ValueError on duplicated, missing, out-of-range and session-straddling partitions, which is the only implementable reading of 'raising on overlapping sessions' under the mandated (n_sessions, trials_per_session) signature.

Tests gate is green and biting. From the repository root `python -m pytest -q` and `pytest -q` both report 40 passed; plain `python tests/test_seedv_split.py` reports 36 and `python test_repro_split_disjoint.py` reports 4. The regression test is at the repository root, is named test_repro_split_disjoint.py, contains test_repro_split_disjoint_covers_every_index_once (disjointness + exact-once coverage) and test_repro_split_keeps_whole_sessions_together, and includes a mutation guard asserting the replacement is not the leaky subset relation and that seed 7 changes membership. Both test files bootstrap the repository root on sys.path, so the console-script import failure the challenge measured does not occur.

Record and hygiene. research/pointer.json names research/seedv-split-repair-caed2113; DIR/research.json has parent, experiment and 11 evidence entries, DIR/report.json has 7 title/evidence pairs, and RESEARCH.md, charter.md, summary.md and round-1.md restate the same numbers as the raw evidence. The three DIR scout JSONs parse and hash to caed2113dff2d182a2ad742f08e1b65a817a1f4ddd2f1a7e819ed9e2b075efb6, matching the chosen hash8. No .fabro-reviews/ or .zeroshot/ directory exists, the notebook and README are unmodified, and only seedv_split.py, tests/test_seedv_split.py and test_repro_split_disjoint.py were added as application files.

Substantive judgement. The retained improvement is applied faithfully to the letters of the audit's retention (whole-session, seeded, pairwise-disjoint, fail-fast, non-empty), the shipped implementation is stdlib-only and O(N), and the record is honest about the limits that matter: the notebook's cell 37 remains leaky because the change is additive and the notebook must not be modified, session-level disjointness is not subject-level disjointness under SEED-V's 16x3 layout, the rectangular (n_sessions, trials_per_session) model cannot express the 7-15 trials/session shape implied by cell 24, and the 0.6/0.2/0.2 default deliberately differs from training_percent=0.8 (348 vs 460 training trials). None of the observed nits affect the correctness of the candidate or the fairness of the measurement, so the verdict is accept.

Copying the three DIR files back byte-identically restores caed2113 and makes the naming rule auditable (verified: the DIR files hash to caed2113dff...).

Scope the 'deviates by at most one session' claim: seedv_split.py's module docstring (honest-limitations paragraph) states the realised split deviates from the requested ratio by at most one session for every input, but that is only true for the default 60/20/20 ratios (I measured a worst case of 0.8 sessions over n_sessions=3..999). The min-one-session repair breaks it for skewed ratios: (0.98,0.01,0.01) at n_sessions=3 returns 1/1/1, a 1.94-session deviation from the 2.94-session train target, and (0.9,0.05,0.05) at n=3 deviates by 1.70. Reword to scope the bound to the default ratios (or state the 'up to one session plus the min-one repair offset' rule) and, if the general claim is kept, add one skewed-ratio case to test_realised_sizes_stay_within_one_session_of_the_target.

Name the serialization used for the reproducibility digest in research.json/report.json/RESEARCH.md: 1b8bc0aaeee1afb6055359e283e3a4625887e84082bfa1fef44b1f0285a612e8 is hashlib.sha256(json.dumps((train, val, test))).hexdigest(); I reproduced it exactly and it is stable under PYTHONHASHSEED 0/1/12345, so this is a documentation correction that makes the evidence independently checkable, not a data correction.
